32487.overview:
The Wizard and the Princess is an arcade adventure split into five stages where your quest is to rescue a Princess from an evil Wizard's castle. Starting with 120 Strength Points and 150 Magic Points you must get to the castle, slay a Dragon, search the castle before escaping with the Princess. You are armed with a sword and some spells where you can throw lightning bolts or fireballs, or put monsters to sleep and slit their throats. When not fighting you can increase your strength or pray for guidance. Each stage have different game styles and they are:

Stage One: On a single screen viewed from above you start on the left of the screen with the castle on the right. You must move across the screen through the hills and flat ground while moving round the trees and mountains. On your journey you will encounter monsters to fight as well as pools to drink from but these can either weaken or strengthen you.

Stage Two: A single screen viewed from the side sees your warrior having to slay a fire breathing Dragon. The Dragon moves around the screen and will stop occasionally to breath out fire and you must avoid the fire and the Dragon to kill it in a sweet spot with your sword.

Stage Three: With the Dragon slayed you must move around a 1st person perspective maze looking for the exit.

Stage Four: Another maze but this time viewed from above as you search various rooms looking for the Princess. You must kill every monster you encounter before the Princess is released. Lightning bolts can be used to remove walls.

Stage Five: You have finally found and rescued the Princess but outside the castle you have more dangers to face before the Princess is safe. Viewed from the side on a single screen, you must cross a bridge while avoiding falling rocks. Once you have crossed the bridge you will face a two-headed monster that needs killing before your quest is over.

164153.overview:
In Wacky Waiters you control a waiter that has to get from one end of the screen to the other to deliver drinks to the beckoning customers waiting there. Each level consists of platforms and elevators and you have to use the elevators to move across the level and up/down platforms.

If you drop into one of the elevator shafts or if the time runs out you are fired. Get fired three times and it's Game Over.

164154.overview: Wall Street is a text-based stock market simulation, where the object is to buy or sell shares in an attempt to make your first million. You can watch the plot of the day's trading within 30 days. During that time period, pressing a key on the keyboard brings up an option screen where you can buy or sell shares, or review your history. At the end of the 30 days, you can either keep going or continue beyond that.

164155.overview: Warrior is a single player only Tron Light Cycles game for the Commodore VIC-20. The game is keyboard control only. It was developed and published by ISCA Software in 1983.

164157.overview:
Wunda Walter! is a fast-paced side-scrolling action game where the player controls a balloon-like character called Walter. The game takes place on the planet Plato where venomous energies called fuzz-balls have created chaos. It is up to Walter to eliminate these things by simply stepping on them.

Walter starts out running on the ground and by holding the joystick button he will rise up in the air. Releasing it again will cause him to fall back towards the ground. The aim of the game is simply to make it across the levels while stepping on as many fuzz-balls as possible. The difficulty of the game comes from the various dangerous objects and rough surfaces that have to be avoided. Any contact with these will cause Walter to burst. Walter has five lives and when they are used up it's game over. There are four levels with different landscapes and obstacles.

164158.overview:
Woodworm Whacker is an arcade-action game, in which you have to shoot evil woodworms while avoiding their shots.

Your weapons is frisbee-like, and it keeps bouncing forth and back/up and down till it hit enough enemies. Be careful, as your weapon can also kill you!

164160.overview: Whodunnit is a murder mystery game for the Commodore VIC-20 which is loosely based on the board game Clue. It was published by Sophisticated Games in 1983. Mind boggling and fiendishly difficult detective game for 1 - 6 players with a genuinely different crime every time. Twelve guests have gathered for drinks at Murder Manor, but by the end of the evening one of them will be dead. To find the murderer you must ask questions, establish movements, motives, alibis etc. Then make your arrest and watch the trial at the Old Bailey to see if you are successfully.

164161.overview: In the 1980s, breakfast cereal manufacturer, Weetabix created a British TV advertising campaign for their cereal, turning the Weetabix biscuits into characters called Dunk, Bixie, Crunch, Brains and Brian. This led to a computer game starring Dunk and his mission is to destroy all the Titchies who have set out to destroy the biscuits themselves. Based on Space Invaders, the game is a single screen shooter viewed from the side with Dunk on the bottom of the screen and the Titchies at the top in formation. The Titchies mainly stay in formation but will occasionally move about the screen elsewhere. Moving left or right, Dunk has to collect a Weetarocket and fire it upwards to remove a Titchie while avoiding the bolts dropped from above. If Dunk is about to get hit by a bolt then he can make his Weet Force Shield appear to remove the bolt. The shield will always appear if a bolt is close to Dunk but if he doesn't make it appear himself then this drains his Neet Weet Energy. Moving about the screen and using rockets also drains his energy and lose it all and it is game over. Once all Titichies have been destroyed then it is onto the next harder and faster level. There are five levels in total and any of these can be selected before the start of the game.

209208.overview:
Title: Wormhole
Platform: 8k expanded Commodore VIC-20
Video: PAL/NTSC
Interface: Joystick only
Game type: Arcade
Written by: W E de Villiers
Copyright: 2022 eXimietas Software

The story: You are an intergalactic pilot transporting passengers across thousands of light-years of space to trading stations on the edge of the known universe. You have to avoid planetoids, small moons and satellites as you navigate towards each wormhole. To get to a trading station, you need to make multiple routing wormhole jumps. Close to many wormholes are teleportation stations, which can transport passengers from nearby ships and moons to the station. So when there is a station near a wormhole you need to dock your ship, teleport and pick up the passengers before continuing on your journey. 

But there is also a problem - there are hostile aliens that will also try to take over the teleportation station. You can shunt these hostiles back to their original location in under a second, but "teleshunting" may be very hazardous to a teleportee's wellbeing, to say the least. So you need to make sure that you only shunt back hostiles and not friendly ticket paying passengers.

217965.overview: Words, Words, Words is an educational game for practising reading and spelling. When starting out the player selects which of the game's eight scenes to begin with. Once moving to the chosen scene the player is shown objects and has to type the correct words. Once an object has been correctly spelled it takes its place in the scene. If all objects in a scene are spelled correctly the scene will come to life through animations. Each scene (except for the castle) ends with the player getting to select the next scene to move to. If an answer is wrong the player gets another chance to get it right, if still wrong the word is spelled out and the game moves on.

218716.overview:
White Line Warrior is a 1-player arcade game for the VIC-20.

You are Obi Wan Wyatt, and just received a message from Astroscan Intelligence that long range scanners detected a large fleet of Red Line Axel Fighters of the Imperial Fleet approaching. Computer analysis of their current course indicates their target is Earth. They will try to obtain the sub-atomic "Spaze" area at the Earth's core. Only the sub-atomic White Line Warriors can stop the invasion.

The player controls a small line on the screen that moves in the cardinal directions. The goal is to move the line as long as possible without hitting the edge of the screen or other lines. The longer the line grows, the more points the player scores. If the line grows long enough, the player advances to a new level with a faster moving line.

395479.overview:
Worm is a game for the VIC-20 in which you play a worm in a maze who has to make your way up to the top of the maze and eat the apple while avoiding the nasties. The game was developed and published by Italian company, WizardSoft. The year of release is currently unknown right now, however.

The in-game text is completely in English.

456408.overview: A game of underwater skill and high-tech battle maneuvers.

463083.overview:
Vital equipment is needed by your allies in order to stop the enemy missiles that are continually attacking your base. This equipment has to be loaded onto your helicopter in daylight and dropped over a target area. Game play is divided into 3 phases.

In Phase 1, the player must take off and defend their fuel lines from enemy missiles. The player takes off from the landing pad, and can move in the cardinal directions to shoot down incoming missiles from the left. Each missile that passes by the player costs 20 fuel. If the player is hit by a missile it's game over.

In Phase 2, the enemy begins to drop parachute mines directly onto your supply lines. The player controls a gun that moves laterally at the bottom of the screen. You must protect your helicopter's fueling by shooting the incoming mines. Each missed mine costs 5 fuel, and if all fuel is lost or the gun is hit by a mine it's game over.

In Phase 3, the player must successfully make the cargo drop with their helicopter while defending from enemy missiles, and return safely to base.
